customConcept.name: Katz's Delicatessen
customConcept.blurb: A cavernous Jewish deli on the Lower East Side since 1888: take a ticket, tip the cutter, and eat a pound of hand-sliced pastrami on rye.

state.circumstances: You run Katz's Delicatessen, open since 1888 on the Lower East Side. The family owns the building. The pastrami recipe hasn't changed in over a century, and you're not about to be the one who changes it.

features.name: The cutting counter
features.pitch: A long counter of carvers hand-slicing to order; you take a ticket at the door and tip your cutter.

features.name: The Ludlow Room
features.pitch: A 68-seat side room sealed off as a walk-in cooler from 1949 until 2026, now reopened for overflow and private events.

features.name: Nationwide shipping
features.pitch: Pastrami, corned beef and salami shipped across the country, a business that goes back to 'Send a Salami to Your Boy in the Army'.

features.name: The famous table
features.pitch: The table from the scene in When Harry Met Sally, with a sign over it.

setting.name: Houston and Ludlow, Lower East Side
setting.desc: On the corner of East Houston and Ludlow Street, under a sign the neighbourhood has used as a landmark for a century. Tourists from every country, New Yorkers who've eaten here all their lives, a late-night crowd from the bars on Ludlow, and a line on the sidewalk most weekends.

ev.text: The holidays: tourists from every direction and lines around the corner onto Ludlow.
The holiday shipping season: pastrami boxes going out to every state.
Beef prices spiked at the packers. Every sandwich costs more to make, and the menu price is already famous.

desk.title: A film crew wants the deli
desk.text: A production company wants to shoot a scene here on a Monday: the whole room for fourteen hours, and the sign in the shot.

choices.label: Rent them the room
choices.blurb: A good fee and another movie for the walls.

desk.title: A developer wants the air rights
desk.text: A developer is offering serious money for more of the air rights over the building. Take it, and the neighbourhood around the sign changes a little more.

kit.model: Existing exhaust fan & duct, no makeup air
A couple of old ABC extinguishers
APW Wyott roller with bun warmer
Full POS: handhelds, kitchen screens & online ordering
Commercial bentwood chairs and laminate-topped tables
A standard set: hotel pans, sheet pans, knives and scales
Smart safe with provisional bank credit

log.text: You run Katz's Delicatessen, open since 1888 on the Lower East Side. The family owns the building. The pastrami recipe hasn't changed in over a century, and you're not about to be the one who changes it.

world.notes: This is Katz's Delicatessen at East Houston and Ludlow on Manhattan's Lower East Side, founded in 1888: a ticket-and-counter deli where cutters hand-carve pastrami, corned beef and brisket cured and smoked in house, famous for the scene in When Harry Met Sally. It serves roughly 30,000 to 40,000 pounds of pastrami a week between the deli and its nationwide shipping business (reports vary), and in 2026 reopened the 68-seat Ludlow Room, used as a walk-in cooler since 1949. Sandwich prices are as recently reported (pastrami $28.95, Reuben $29.95, combo $30.95). The deli's sales, seat count and property value are estimates, and staff names are invented; the player is not the real owner.

United States.mealTimes: Lunch around noon to 1pm, dinner from about 6 to 8pm.
United States.customs: Guests expect fast, attentive service, free tap water and refills, and a check brought on request. Tipping 18-22% is expected at table service.
United States.labour: At-will employment in most states; overtime after 40 hours a week; minimum wages set by state and city.
